20.en: "The foulest rot is corruption that seeps down from on high."

38.en: Maintain the status quo within the Imperium at any cost.

46.en: No one is beyond reproach, be it planetary governors or the lowliest hab rat.

54.en: Death to the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.GPqYZykonC12TJb1.JournalEntryPage.5jO3tXI5hSEBAC4s]{Infractionist}, the revolutionary, and the heretic.

76.en: Seek out heresies within the Imperium’s factions and ruling classes. Corruption from within is the greatest threat to the status quo, so purge extensively when it is found. Maintaining the Imperium’s long-term stability is worth any cost, so sacrifices should be made across all levels of society and rule.

82.en: Libricaranism is a relatively new philosophy borne in the Calixis Sector. Its adherents believe maintaining the Imperium and the smooth running of its various factions is of supreme importance, and the key to this is ensuring good leadership. If the rulers of planets and organisations across the Imperium were freed from corruption, then the Imperium would be both pure and efficient.

86.en: A Radical offshoot of the @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians}, Libricars also believe in the perfection of the GodEmperor’s plan but fear it has already been corrupted by the greed and corruption of those in power. Since @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.X5EFP7IgIUx6CaBW]{Lord Solar Macharius}’s death, the rule of the sector has degraded to the point that some Libricars claim a complete overhaul of the local powers is required. Such claims infuriate Amalathians, and Inquisitors of these two philosophies continually clash.

90.en: Libricars seek out the slightest taint or indiscretion in the ruling classes and purge the Imperium of any corrupt individuals. They blame rulers for evidence of corruption within the planet or organisation they rule, so not only do they destroy a cult when they find it, but they execute the rulers who let the cult take root.

94.en: Their extreme methods of purification make them unpopular. Like @UUID[.yds9IfgKQlwxLqq6]{Monodominants}, Libricars are known for being overzealous and are quick to resort to drastic measures, such as

114.en: The Libricar philosophy demands that adherents be unyielding and ruthless. Inquisitors expect the same from their acolytes — when wielding extreme measures, they do not expect their authority to be questioned.

122.en: Knowing, and likely experiencing in the past, that heresy can take root even within the ruling classes of Imperial society, Libricars have little patience or respect for people in positions of power.

130.en: Libricars know that the greatest threat to their plans is the oversight of other Inquisitors. They are always wary of being spied on, and so typically distance themselves from the rest of the Inquisition or their Ordo. They will not tolerate dissent or any hint of betrayal from those within their retinue.

144.en: The Inquisitor’s Interrogator, Naevea Green, was sent to usurp the Planetary Governor of Calicot and install less corrupt, more malleable leadership. But the Interrogator deemed herself the only suitable candidate, installing herself and enacting martial law. Clean up Green’s mess and extract her before the populace rises against her and the Inquisition loses its hold on the planet.

152.en: The Governor of Hive Forlan on Desperion has been assassinated. The nobility is pointing to rampant infractionism supposedly led by heretical cults. But intel reports that the Forlan Goods & Services criminal cartel is based there and may be involved. Stability on Desperion must be reasserted — assess the local powers, ensure the most beneficial ruler is put in place, and purge the rest.
